text: ds-harness-remote 是面向 DSH Desktop、Web、Android 与 dsh-TUI Host 的远程访问插件，通过 DSH 插件入口、侧边栏和 TUI 命令连接远程 Harness 工作区。它可发现在线 Host 与工作区，并在已连接的 Harness 工作区中列出、阅读、创建和等待会话，也支持发送任务、上传或下载文件及查看操作回执。适合需要从另一台设备继续访问工作电脑上 Harness 会话的用户。使用时需配置 Remote Server 并登录账户；具体客户端和后端能力取决于部署配置。

ds-harness-remote connects DSH to remote Harness workspaces. It discovers Hosts and workspaces, lists and reads sessions, sends tasks, waits for status, transfers files, and retrieves operation receipts. Use it to access Harness from another device. A Remote Server account is required.
想从手机或另一台电脑继续用工作电脑上的 DSH 会话。
能不能远程查看有哪些 Harness 主机和工作区？
我想从外部设备查看远程会话记录和运行状态。
如何给远程 Harness 会话发送任务并等它完成？
I need to access my DSH Harness workspaces from another device.
Can I inspect and manage sessions running on a remote Harness host?
「远程主机与工作区发现」：列出账户可访问的在线 Host，并读取指定 Host 上可用的 Harness、Codex 与 ACP 工作区。由 DSH 工具调用触发，返回主机和工作区目录。
「远程 Harness 会话管理」：查看会话列表、历史与状态，创建会话、发送任务、等待状态变化或请求中断。通过已注册的远程会话工具按 Host、工作区和会话标识操作。
「远程文件传输」：将本机文件上传到 Harness 会话工作区，或将工作区文件下载到运行插件的安装位置。通过上传和下载会话工具触发，返回文件路径及字节数。
需要 Remote Server 账户；会话操作连接所选 Host。（见 packages/plugin/src/remote-session-tools.ts:72）

Return to the same Harness session from whichever device is with you.

text:
ds-harness-remote README · Features：- Access your local Harness instance remotely from the web, a PC, or a mobile device: DSH first, with Codex, Cursor, and Antigravity support too.
- Use the native DeepSeek Harness interface without a separate desktop conversation UI.
- Create workspaces, configure models, and switch conversation models with the same smooth workflow as local use.
- Support DeepSeek Harness Desktop, ready to use after installation.
- Run a terminal-only [dsh-TUI](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI) profile as a Host.
- No public listening port or public IP is required on the Harness Host. Connect from anywhere with internet access over a bidirectional end-to-end encrypted channel.
- Prefer P2P connections, use TURN relay nodes worldwide, and fall back to Server Relay when needed.
- Access workspace files, read-only previews, remote terminals, and authorized local development-service previews through the native Harness sidebar.
- CodeX and ACP terminals use the Host's default shell in the session directory and restore the terminal screen on reconnect.
- Android keeps per-conversation drafts and reading positions, offers backend-separated search
  and local favor

ds-harness-remote README · DeepSeek Harness Desktop support：Open **Extensions / Plugin management** in DeepSeek Harness Desktop, choose installation
from npm, and enter this package:

`ds-harness-remote@0.5.22`

Restart Desktop afterward. Its official `dsh` launcher can also install the pinned package
with `dsh plugin --profile desktop add -w ds-harness-remote@0.5.22`.

ds-harness-remote README · dsh-TUI Host：For terminal Host setup with [dsh-TUI](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI), see the
[dsh-TUI Remote guide](docs/dsh-tui.md).

ds-harness-remote README · Command-line installation：Add the exact package version through DSH's plugin manager for the `web` profile:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add -w ds-harness-remote@0.5.22
```

Restart DeepSeek Harness after installation.

For CLI installation, use `dsh plugin` to install the npm package into the selected profile
and add its bundle configuration layer.

ds-harness-remote README · Plugin installer：- **Linux:** requires root; reuses an existing DSH or bootstraps private Node.js/DSH, accepts a one-time Host registration token, and enables/starts a systemd system service. The Host and remote tools run as **root**; grant access only to trusted accounts.
- **macOS:** run as a normal user; reuses Desktop's official launcher or an existing CLI, without installing DSH or creating services.
- Windows users use official Plugin management or existing Harness commands; no Windows installer is provided.

ds-harness-remote README · Plugin installer：See the [installation guide](docs/installation.md) for private token input, updates, service controls and validation limits. Repository changes do not automatically deploy the hosted installer.

ds-harness-remote README · Recommended companion: Intelligent UI：[Intelligent UI](https://github.com/dreamfarer-space/deepseek-harness-intelligent-ui) lets the model answer
with cards, tables, charts and forms. The Android client renders them natively, and lists the plugin under
**Plugins → Remote ready**, where you can switch it on or off and edit its live settings.

Install it on the computer, **into the same profile as Remote** (plugins cannot be installed from the phone):

ds-harness-remote README · Recommended companion: Intelligent UI：| Host | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Desktop | Plugin management → install from npm → `deepseek-harness-intelligent-ui` |
| CLI `web` profile | `dsh plugin --profile web add -w deepseek-harness-intelligent-ui` |
| `scripts/install.sh` | `INTELLIGENT_UI=1` (optionally `INTELLIGENT_UI_VERSION=...`) |

Restart that Harness instance afterward. Editing its settings from the phone needs Intelligent UI 0.2.10 or later.

ds-harness-remote README · Android client：Keep conversations connected across multiple workspaces at once, and use **Bot mode**, powered by [Fei2411/DS-Bot](https://github.com/Fei2411/DS-Bot).

Download the latest APK from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/liguobao/ds-harness-remote/releases/latest), sign in to the same account, and select a Host and workspace to continue your conversation.

ds-harness-remote README · Quick start：1. Open **Remote** from the Harness sidebar.
2. Sign in using a Server-provided OAuth QR-code method, or use your account and password. The provider list is loaded dynamically; new Server integrations need no further plugin release.
3. The Host starts with control of the current computer enabled. Remote terminal access is also enabled by default; you can turn it off in the detailed Remote settings.
4. On another device, open the DeepSeek Harness desktop edition, Remote Web, or the Android client and sign in to the same account.
5. Select the online Host, then choose an existing workspace or browse remote directories to open one.

ds-harness-remote README · Quick start：By default, Remote uses this project's hosted Server at [https://dsh.r2049.cn](https://dsh.r2049.cn).

For self-hosting, use the repository's [minimal Server](apps/server/README.md); its Web page shows device status only.

ds-harness-remote README · Desktop：The current computer starts with **Allow control of this device** enabled and is available as a Host. Remote terminal access is also enabled by default and can be turned off in the Host's detailed Remote settings. On another computer, select an online Host and open one of its workspaces.
ds-harness-remote README · Desktop：The workspace opens in the native Harness interface, with the active Host and encrypted connection status shown in the header.

ds-harness-remote README · Android：Use text or image prompts, switch models, and access supported workspace files and terminals. The interface follows the system language and supports English, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Spanish, German, and French. In language settings, tap “More ...” to show all languages. See the [Android guide](apps/android/README.md) for details.

ds-harness-remote README · Android：

Mobile Settings includes a global **Compact conversations** switch, off by default and applied when a conversation is next opened.
ds-harness-remote README · Android：Supporting Hosts reduce historical tool details while preserving messages and tool status. Turn the setting off and reopen the conversation to load full history.

ds-harness-remote README · How it works：```text
DSH Desktop / Remote Web / Android
  ↔ authenticated, end-to-end encrypted channel
Remote Plugin on the Host
  ↔ supported Harness or optional Codex workspace support

The Harness Host does not need a public listening port. You can connect from anywhere with internet access.

Remote communicates over a bidirectional end-to-end encrypted channel and switches the client to the selected Host's native Harness API.

The original workspace, tools, and permission flow remain on that computer.

ds-harness-remote README · How it works：Every settings namespace currently registered by the Host can also be configured remotely through the official Harness settings API.

Credential values remain write-only, and Host-local document/open actions are never exposed.

ds-harness-remote README · Experimental ACP workspaces：The Host runs local AI backends and forwards prompts, streamed replies and approvals through the encrypted Remote channel.

Desktop and Android project their workspaces and sessions into the existing interface in memory, without writing them to Harness storage.

Supported backends:

ds-harness-remote README · Experimental ACP workspaces：- **Codex** — connected through its independent App Server interface, with the same workspace entry.
- **Cursor** — connected through the CLI's ACP interface.
- **Antigravity (AGY)** — its stream-json CLI is adapted to the ACP gateway.
- **Pi Agent (experimental)** — install `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` and `pi-acp` on the Host, configure Pi's provider locally; Remote automatically detects and initializes Pi unless explicitly disabled in Remote settings. The workspace is available only after ACP initialization succeeds. Uses the separate ACP data plane. Tools run with Host-user permissions; per-tool confirmation requires a Pi extension and is not enabled by default.

ds-harness-remote README · Experimental ACP workspaces：- **OpenCode** — connected through `opencode acp`, with workspace discovery and history recovery. Host startup checks the CLI's supported options, accepting both native-listener and stdio-only ACP builds. Native session archiving on Desktop/Android requires the authenticated loopback API; builds without it report archiving unavailable. Archive state is saved by OpenCode; history is retained. Unarchive is not yet exposed.
- **Claude** — uses a locally authorized `claude-agent-acp` on the Host; enable it in Remote settings. Desktop/Android support workspaces, history, text prompts and approvals. Image input and direct Files/Terminal access are not available.

ds-harness-remote README · Experimental ACP workspaces：Setup and adapter development: [Agent workspace integration guide](docs/acp-integration.md).

Model selection for Cursor, Claude, Pi, OpenCode, and AGY on Desktop/Android uses the Host's actual model catalog and waits for backend confirmation.

Reasoning effort options depend on what the backend provides. Cursor uses a separate process per session, so model changes do not affect other conversations.

ds-harness-remote README · End-to-end encryption：Harness business traffic is encrypted on the Client and decrypted only by the selected Host using the fixed `Noise_IK_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256` suite.

Connections must pass both same-account membership and locally pinned device identity key checks.

The service can coordinate connections and observe necessary network metadata, but it cannot read session messages, prompts, tool output, workspace paths, or remote file contents.
ds-harness-remote README · End-to-end encryption：See [End-to-end encryption](docs/end-to-end-encryption.md) for the handshake, key lifecycle, visible metadata, replay protection, and security limits.

ds-harness-remote README · Network and transport：The Host opens outbound connections only; it does not listen on a public port or require router port forwarding.

Remote negotiates paths in the order `LAN -> P2P -> TURN -> Relay`.

When WebRTC is unavailable or cannot connect, it falls back to the encrypted WebSocket Relay.

Every path carries the same Noise ciphertext and keeps the same Host/Client identity boundary.

ds-harness-remote README · Network and transport：See [Network and transport](docs/network.md) for the topology, control and data planes, NAT behavior, fallback, reconnect semantics, and current validation status.

ds-harness-remote README · Security：- Session traffic is end-to-end encrypted. The service relays ciphertext without storing session plaintext or device private keys.
- Server membership and the Host's locally pinned peer identity must both authorize a connection.
- [Remote Tools injection](docs/remote-tools.md) — optional `remote_*` session tools; disabled by default and enabled from detailed Remote settings.

ds-harness-remote README · Security：- Interactive terminals use the Host-local `terminal.enabled` switch (on by default). They run as the Host user, independently of Agent approvals.
- General tool RPC and remote desktop are not exposed.
- The workspace picker lists folders only and returns bounded, read-only directory metadata.
- Remote file preview cannot write, delete, upload, execute, or open a path in an external application.
- Codex Remote / Agent ACP is optional, can be disabled, and follows the same encrypted Host permission boundary as the rest of Remote.
- Removing a device revokes its credentials, membership, and active Remote connections.

ds-harness-remote README · FAQ：**Do I need a public IP or port forwarding?**

No. The Host only opens outbound connections and never listens on a public port.

**Can the service read my conversations?**

No. The service relays ciphertext only. Routing, authorization, presence and rate limiting require control metadata such as account and device ownership, online status, connection times and `connectionId`; prompts, conversation content, tool input and output, workspace paths and file preview contents stay unreadable.

ds-harness-remote README · FAQ：**Which machine can act as a Host?**

Any Harness instance with the Remote plugin installed and signed in. The `web`, `desktop` and dsh-TUI profiles can all act as a Host, and command-line installation uses `web` by default. The installer never creates a Web service automatically for `headless`, SDK or dsh-TUI profiles, so a dsh-TUI Host manages its own process.

**Can several devices connect to one Host at the same time?**

ds-harness-remote README · FAQ：Yes. Multiple clients can connect concurrently, with RPC calls and streams isolated per connection.

**Which Harness versions are supported?**

The current baseline is `dsh-v0.2.1-rc.1`, compatible with `0.2.0` rc.2 / rc.1. See the [compatibility guide](docs/compatibility.md).

ds-harness-remote README · FAQ：Harness `0.1.1-rc.2` ApiProxy support has been removed from the Host plugin, its bundled Remote client, and Android. Use a Host with the official Typert Remote carrier; Hosts that only provide ApiProxy or lack capability discovery are rejected, with no fallback.

CodeX/ACP keep their independent data planes, and Desktop projections use Typert in memory.

**Why does the Linux installer require root?**

ds-harness-remote README · FAQ：It configures a systemd system service, so the Host, Agent tools and remote terminals run with root privileges. Only expose it to trusted accounts.

**Can I install the iOS app directly?**

It is in TestFlight beta today and not publicly released; see [issue #20](https://github.com/liguobao/ds-harness-remote/issues/20).

**How is this different from frp, a tunnel, or remote desktop?**

ds-harness-remote README · FAQ：Conventional server-based TCP port forwarding routes traffic through a Server, making its bandwidth a potential bottleneck.

This project probes four connection modes in sequence to establish P2P connections even in complex network environments.

Remote desktop captures the entire computer screen and reproduces it on the client, placing demands on upload and download bandwidth as well as computer performance.

ds-harness-remote README · FAQ：This project encrypts and transmits only the messages needed by the native Harness conversation interface. General tool RPC and desktop control are not exposed, and permissions and approvals remain on the Host.

ds-harness-remote README · How it works：```text
DSH Desktop / Remote Web / Android
  ↔ authenticated, end-to-end encrypted channel
Remote Plugin on the Host
  ↔ supported Harness or optional Codex workspace support

The Harness Host does not need a public listening port. You can connect from anywhere with internet access.

Remote communicates over a bidirectional end-to-end encrypted channel and switches the client to the selected Host's native Harness API.

The original workspace, tools, and permission flow remain on that computer.

ds-harness-remote README · How it works：Every settings namespace currently registered by the Host can also be configured remotely through the official Harness settings API.

Credential values remain write-only, and Host-local document/open actions are never exposed.

ds-harness-remote README · Experimental ACP workspaces：The Host runs local AI backends and forwards prompts, streamed replies and approvals through the encrypted Remote channel.

Desktop and Android project their workspaces and sessions into the existing interface in memory, without writing them to Harness storage.

Supported backends:

ds-harness-remote README · Experimental ACP workspaces：- **Codex** — connected through its independent App Server interface, with the same workspace entry.
- **Cursor** — connected through the CLI's ACP interface.
- **Antigravity (AGY)** — its stream-json CLI is adapted to the ACP gateway.
- **Pi Agent (experimental)** — install `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` and `pi-acp` on the Host, configure Pi's provider locally; Remote automatically detects and initializes Pi unless explicitly disabled in Remote settings. The workspace is available only after ACP initialization succeeds. Uses the separate ACP data plane. Tools run with Host-user permissions; per-tool confirmation requires a Pi extension and is not enabled by default.

ds-harness-remote README · Experimental ACP workspaces：- **OpenCode** — connected through `opencode acp`, with workspace discovery and history recovery. Host startup checks the CLI's supported options, accepting both native-listener and stdio-only ACP builds. Native session archiving on Desktop/Android requires the authenticated loopback API; builds without it report archiving unavailable. Archive state is saved by OpenCode; history is retained. Unarchive is not yet exposed.
- **Claude** — uses a locally authorized `claude-agent-acp` on the Host; enable it in Remote settings. Desktop/Android support workspaces, history, text prompts and approvals. Image input and direct Files/Terminal access are not available.

ds-harness-remote README · Experimental ACP workspaces：Setup and adapter development: [Agent workspace integration guide](docs/acp-integration.md).

Model selection for Cursor, Claude, Pi, OpenCode, and AGY on Desktop/Android uses the Host's actual model catalog and waits for backend confirmation.

Reasoning effort options depend on what the backend provides. Cursor uses a separate process per session, so model changes do not affect other conversations.

ds-harness-remote README · End-to-end encryption：Harness business traffic is encrypted on the Client and decrypted only by the selected Host using the fixed `Noise_IK_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256` suite.

Connections must pass both same-account membership and locally pinned device identity key checks.

The service can coordinate connections and observe necessary network metadata, but it cannot read session messages, prompts, tool output, workspace paths, or remote file contents.
ds-harness-remote README · End-to-end encryption：See [End-to-end encryption](docs/end-to-end-encryption.md) for the handshake, key lifecycle, visible metadata, replay protection, and security limits.

ds-harness-remote README · Network and transport：The Host opens outbound connections only; it does not listen on a public port or require router port forwarding.

Remote negotiates paths in the order `LAN -> P2P -> TURN -> Relay`.

When WebRTC is unavailable or cannot connect, it falls back to the encrypted WebSocket Relay.

Every path carries the same Noise ciphertext and keeps the same Host/Client identity boundary.

ds-harness-remote README · Network and transport：See [Network and transport](docs/network.md) for the topology, control and data planes, NAT behavior, fallback, reconnect semantics, and current validation status.

ds-harness-remote README · Security：- Session traffic is end-to-end encrypted. The service relays ciphertext without storing session plaintext or device private keys.
- Server membership and the Host's locally pinned peer identity must both authorize a connection.
- [Remote Tools injection](docs/remote-tools.md) — optional `remote_*` session tools; disabled by default and enabled from detailed Remote settings.

ds-harness-remote README · Security：- Interactive terminals use the Host-local `terminal.enabled` switch (on by default). They run as the Host user, independently of Agent approvals.
- General tool RPC and remote desktop are not exposed.
- The workspace picker lists folders only and returns bounded, read-only directory metadata.
- Remote file preview cannot write, delete, upload, execute, or open a path in an external application.
- Codex Remote / Agent ACP is optional, can be disabled, and follows the same encrypted Host permission boundary as the rest of Remote.
- Removing a device revokes its credentials, membership, and active Remote connections.

ds-harness-remote README · FAQ：**Do I need a public IP or port forwarding?**

No. The Host only opens outbound connections and never listens on a public port.

**Can the service read my conversations?**

No. The service relays ciphertext only. Routing, authorization, presence and rate limiting require control metadata such as account and device ownership, online status, connection times and `connectionId`; prompts, conversation content, tool input and output, workspace paths and file preview contents stay unreadable.

ds-harness-remote README · FAQ：**Which machine can act as a Host?**

Any Harness instance with the Remote plugin installed and signed in. The `web`, `desktop` and dsh-TUI profiles can all act as a Host, and command-line installation uses `web` by default. The installer never creates a Web service automatically for `headless`, SDK or dsh-TUI profiles, so a dsh-TUI Host manages its own process.

**Can several devices connect to one Host at the same time?**

ds-harness-remote README · FAQ：Yes. Multiple clients can connect concurrently, with RPC calls and streams isolated per connection.

**Which Harness versions are supported?**

The current baseline is `dsh-v0.2.1-rc.1`, compatible with `0.2.0` rc.2 / rc.1. See the [compatibility guide](docs/compatibility.md).

ds-harness-remote README · FAQ：Harness `0.1.1-rc.2` ApiProxy support has been removed from the Host plugin, its bundled Remote client, and Android. Use a Host with the official Typert Remote carrier; Hosts that only provide ApiProxy or lack capability discovery are rejected, with no fallback.

CodeX/ACP keep their independent data planes, and Desktop projections use Typert in memory.

**Why does the Linux installer require root?**

ds-harness-remote README · FAQ：It configures a systemd system service, so the Host, Agent tools and remote terminals run with root privileges. Only expose it to trusted accounts.

**Can I install the iOS app directly?**

It is in TestFlight beta today and not publicly released; see [issue #20](https://github.com/liguobao/ds-harness-remote/issues/20).

**How is this different from frp, a tunnel, or remote desktop?**

ds-harness-remote README · FAQ：Conventional server-based TCP port forwarding routes traffic through a Server, making its bandwidth a potential bottleneck.

This project probes four connection modes in sequence to establish P2P connections even in complex network environments.

Remote desktop captures the entire computer screen and reproduces it on the client, placing demands on upload and download bandwidth as well as computer performance.

ds-harness-remote README · FAQ：This project encrypts and transmits only the messages needed by the native Harness conversation interface. General tool RPC and desktop control are not exposed, and permissions and approvals remain on the Host.
